title: Dingjin Chu
text:
👋 Hello, this is Dingjin.
I am a PhD student studying forest disturbance and landscape change using satellite remote sensing and large-scale geospatial data. I work with time-series satellite imagery, Google Earth Engine, and statistical modeling to understand how forests respond to climate variability and human disturbance.
I received my BSc in Forestry from Your University. My research interests sit at the intersection of forest ecology, remote sensing, and environmental data science.

title: About
text:
I am a researcher specializing in forest disturbance and geospatial analysis. My work combines remote sensing, statistical modeling, and large-scale environmental data to understand how forests respond to natural and human-driven disturbances.
I am comfortable working across the full analysis pipeline — from raw satellite imagery and cloud-based processing in Google Earth Engine, to statistical modeling and visualization in R and Python.

title: Projects
text:
A selection of research and data projects. Source code and write-ups are linked where available.



Quantifying forest loss trends and drivers across large spatial extents using time-series satellite imagery. The workflow integrates Hansen Global Forest Change data with climate and topographic covariates to attribute disturbance to fire, harvest, and insect outbreak.
Tools: R, Google Earth Engine, tidyverse




Interactive and static maps for communicating spatial patterns in environmental datasets. Projects include animated time-series maps of vegetation indices and choropleth visualizations of disturbance rates by ecoregion.
Tools: R (ggplot2, tmap, Leaflet), Python (Matplotlib, Folium)




Investigating how interannual climate variability (temperature, precipitation, drought indices) drives fluctuations in forest productivity as measured by MODIS NDVI and GPP products.
Tools: Python, R, netCDF4, xarray
